paras: The whitecapping of John Lee was a reported attack by whitecaps on John Lee, a Black teamster in Virginia and a prospective defense witness for the condemned Doc Bacon, on the night of Saturday, September 12, 1903. Lee was not seen afterward and was supposed to have left the county. The report reached the Richmond Times-Dispatch through Bacon's brother, Charles Bacon, who said that witnesses useful to the defense were being driven out of the county.

Doc Bacon had been convicted of an attempted criminal assault on Mrs. C. E. Geoghegan at Chase City on the night of July 23, and in September he was under a respite from Governor Montague and held in the jail at Petersburg. Among the evidence against him was meal that witnesses said they saw on his hat and head the morning after the attack. In a letter dated September 7, Geoghegan's husband wrote that 'two negroes and a white boy' were expected to testify that 'one John Lee' had thrown flour, not meal, on Bacon five days before the assault, though he argued this could not explain the meal.

On September 15 Charles Bacon, accompanied by the Rev. J. B. Ferrell, visited his brother in the Petersburg jail. He told the paper's Petersburg correspondent that 'all the witnesses who would be of use to Doc Bacon are being driven out of the county.' Jennie Scott, described as 'a colored woman' who had tried to collect money on Bacon's behalf, was said to have been run out of the county and to be in Richmond.

Lee, 'a colored teamster, who said he threw the flour on Bacon,' was 'reported to have been white-capped Saturday night' and had not been seen since. The account gave the 'summition' [supposition] that he too had left the county, but it did not say who the whitecappers were, how many there were, what they did to Lee or where it happened.

No report of an arrest or investigation of the whitecapping appears in the coverage, and nothing later was found on Lee's whereabouts. Charles Bacon planned to stay in Petersburg for a few days, while 'several colored men' solicited subscriptions to pay a lawyer to prosecute an appeal.

The Times-Dispatch printed the item on September 16 in its Petersburg column under the headline 'In Behalf of Doc Bacon' and the deck 'Claim That His Witnesses Are Being Run Out of the County,' alongside notes on a workman's fall and a lodge visit. It attributed the charge to Charles Bacon and presented Lee's whitecapping as a report rather than an established fact. A week earlier the same paper had printed Geoghegan's letter, which named Lee only as the subject of expected new testimony. The Petersburg item is the only account of the whitecapping found in either the white or the Black press.
